Refrigerator.mechanism: A blocked/restricted condenser coil forces the compressor to work harder and run hotter -- documented as one of the leading precursors to compressor failure in commercial refrigeration.
A failing fan reduces airflow across the coil, producing the same overheating stress on the compressor as a blocked coil.

AC.mechanism: Same mechanism as refrigeration: a blocked/restricted coil raises discharge temperature and stresses the compressor.
A clogged filter restricts airflow, forcing the compressor to run under higher load for longer periods.

Washing Machine.mechanism: A seizing or struggling drain pump stalls the drum via the belt-driven system, straining the belt -- a documented failure chain in washer diagnostics.
A slipping/worn belt makes the motor spin without transferring power to the drum, and sustained slipping generates heat that stresses the motor.

Water Heater.mechanism: A depleted anode rod accelerates corrosion and sediment buildup, which insulates and damages the heating element -- 'sediment heavily buries the lower element, dry-firing it.'
Once the anode rod depletes, unchecked corrosion and sediment can force the burner to overheat weakened tank walls, escalating pressure-relief-valve risk.

Microwave.mechanism: Defective interlock switches or a misaligned door are a leading documented cause of a blown fuse.
A shorted magnetron creates dangerous electrical conditions; the fuse sacrifices itself to protect the rest of the unit from cascading damage.

Water Purifier.mechanism: Old and clogged filters strain the entire system and increase pressure load on the pump, a documented precursor to pump damage.
A saturated sediment pre-filter lets contaminants pass through directly to the membrane, leading to fouling/scaling damage.
